theme: The 5 questions every HR/marketing leader should ask before signing an event production contract

linkedin.text:
Before you sign with a corporate event production company, ask them this:

"Walk me through the production run sheet from an event like ours."

Not the proposal deck. Not the case study PDF.

The actual, time-coded, role-assigned run sheet.

Here's why it matters:

→ It tells you immediately whether they treat events as logistics or as managed experiences.
→ It shows you how they think about contingency — not whether they mention it, but where it lives in the document.
→ It reveals the real team structure. The names on a run sheet are the people who will be in your room.

In 16 years of producing 1,500+ corporate events across 130+ destinations, the fastest way to lose our confidence in a potential client's readiness is when they've never asked this question.

And the fastest way a client earns our best work is when they ask it first.

What's the one question you always ask before commissioning a major event? I'm genuinely curious — different industries, different tells. Drop it below.

instagram.text:
Slide 1: 5 questions to ask before you sign with any event production company. (Most buyers only ask 2.) →
Slide 2: Q1 — 'What's your backup plan if the main AV system fails on the day?' A real answer takes 30 seconds. A vague one takes 3 minutes.
Slide 3: Q2 — 'Who exactly will be on-site, and what's their specific role?' The team on the proposal isn't always the team in the room.
Slide 4: Q3 — 'Can I speak directly to the production manager from our last 3 events?' Not the account manager. The producer.
Slide 5: Q4 — 'How do you handle a brief that changes 10 days before the event?' The answer reveals how they actually operate under pressure.
Slide 6: Q5 — 'What outcome did the client measure 60 days after the event?' If they don't know, the event was just logistics.
Slide 7: We've been on the receiving end of all 5 — for 16 years, 1,500+ events, 130+ destinations, 25,000+ participants. Ask us anything. DM open.

facebook.text:
If you're an HR or marketing leader about to brief an event production company, one question separates the vendors who will deliver from the ones who will disappoint:

"Can you show me the production run sheet from a similar event you delivered in the last 12 months?"

Not the proposal. Not the mood board. The actual run sheet.

A production company that has genuinely done the work can pull that in 24 hours. One that leans on renders and references cannot.

We've spent 16 years and 1,500+ events earning the kind of answer that comes without hesitation.

Planning something soon? Ask us. We'll send you exactly that — and walk you through it.
